title: The exterior product of cycle classes passes to rational equivalence in both variables
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology and Chern Classes)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The statement is that the exterior product map CH_n(X) tensor CH_m(Y) -> CH_{n+m}(X x_k Y) is well defined (statement lines 14136-14141), which is not formal because the product is first defined only on cycles: for locally finite families of integral closed subschemes the author forms alpha x beta = sum n_i m_j [X_i x_k Y_j]_{n+m}, which is a cycle (proof lines 14144-14156). The substance is the compatibility with rational equivalence in each variable, and the proof obtains it by realising the product with a fixed class as a bivariant operation: for an integral closed subscheme i : X' -> X of dimension n the flat pullback along X' -> Spec(k) is a class (p')^* in A^{-n}(X' -> Spec(k)) and its composite with i_* is a class c' in A^{-n}(X -> Spec(k)), whose cap product sends an integral Y' of dimension m to [X' x_k Y']_{n+m}, so the construction factors through rational equivalence in the second variable, and symmetry gives the first variable (proof lines 14161-14179). Turning the compatibility into a statement about a bivariant operation rather than checking rational equivalence by hand is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
